items.title: New Date for the Piano Recital
items.text:
Subject: New Date for the Piano Recital

Dear students and families,

I am sorry to tell you that our spring recital must move. The roof of the concert hall is leaking, and the repairs will take a week. The new date is Sunday, June 8, at two o'clock. The place is the same. The tickets you already bought will still work. They are good for the new date. Students who play first should arrive thirty minutes early to warm up. Everyone else may come ten minutes before their turn. If you cannot come on June 8, please tell me by Friday, and I will try to change the order of performers. Thank you for being so understanding.

Best wishes,
Ms. Ahn

qs.q: Why did Ms. Ahn write this email?
o: To thank the performers after a concert
To tell families about a new date
To invite new students to join her lessons
To ask families to buy tickets for a new hall
qs.why: 리사이틀 날짜가 바뀌었음을 알리는 이메일이에요. “The new date is Sunday, June 8.”

qs.q: Why was the recital moved?
o: The hall has a leaking roof.
Ms. Ahn will be away on a trip.
The performers asked for more practice time.
qs.why: “The roof of the concert hall is leaking, and the repairs will take a week.” 지붕이 새서 수리가 필요해요.

qs.q: In the email, the phrase “so understanding” means being ___.
qs.why: “Thank you for being so understanding”은 날짜 변경이라는 문제를 너그럽게 받아들여 준 것에 대한 감사예요. understanding은 ‘이해심 있는, 너그러운’이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “They” in “They are good for the new date” refers to
qs.why: 앞 문장 “The tickets you already bought will still work.”의 tickets를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Which student will most likely arrive at 1:30 p.m. on June 8?
qs.why: 리사이틀은 2시에 시작하고, “Students who play first should arrive thirty minutes early”이므로 첫 연주자가 1시 30분쯤 도착해요.

items.title: Library Floor Repairs
items.text:
Notice to Visitors

The Greenfield Branch Library will close for repairs from Monday, November 3, to Friday, November 14. During this time, workers will put new floors in the reading rooms and the children's area. The building will be noisy, and for safety, visitors cannot enter. Books that are due during the closing will not get late fees. You may return them when we open again on Monday, November 17. If you need a book urgently, please visit the Riverside Branch, which is a ten-minute bus ride away. It will be open as usual, with longer hours on weekends. We apologize for the trouble and thank you for your patience. We promise the new floors will make the library safer and quieter.

qs.q: What is the notice mainly about?
o: A temporary closing of a library
A sale of old books by a library
A new bus route to a library
A contest for the young readers
qs.why: 공사 때문에 도서관이 임시로 문을 닫는다는 안내문이에요.

qs.q: When will the Greenfield Branch Library open again?
qs.why: “when we open again on Monday, November 17.” 14일은 휴관의 마지막 날이에요.

qs.q: What will a person who needs a book on November 6 probably have to do?
o: Ask for a room in the children's area
Pay a late fee at the front desk
Wait at the entrance for the workers
qs.why: 급하게 책이 필요하면 “please visit the Riverside Branch”라고 했으니 다른 도서관에 가야 해요.

qs.q: In the notice, “urgently” is closest in meaning to
qs.why: “need a book urgently”는 ‘급하게, 빨리’ 필요하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “It” in “It will be open as usual” refers to
qs.why: 바로 앞의 “the Riverside Branch”를 가리키며, 그곳은 평소처럼 연다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: My First Kimchi
items.text: Last weekend, my grandfather taught me how to make kimchi. I thought it would be easy, but I was wrong. First, we cut the cabbage in half and covered the leaves with salt. We waited two hours, and then we washed the cabbage carefully. Meanwhile, I mixed red pepper powder, garlic, and ginger into a thick paste. It made my hands red and hot, so Grandpa gave me plastic gloves. Spreading the paste between every leaf took a long time. When we finished, my back was sore. Grandpa laughed and said that patience is the secret ingredient. We put the jar in a cool place, and now I am eager to taste the result in a few days.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this blog post?
o: Kimchi tastes much better without any ginger.
Cabbage must always be washed for two hours.
Plastic gloves are the secret ingredient of kimchi.
Making kimchi with a grandparent was hard but rewarding.
qs.why: 할아버지와 김치를 담그며 힘들었지만 보람 있었던 경험을 이야기해요.

qs.q: What did the writer and Grandpa do after covering the cabbage with salt?
o: They mixed the paste with ginger.
They spread the paste between the leaves.
They put the jar in a cool place.
qs.why: “We waited two hours, and then we washed the cabbage.” 소금을 뿌린 뒤 두 시간을 기다렸어요.

qs.q: Why did Grandpa give the writer plastic gloves?
o: The writer wanted to look like a real cook.
The jar was too slippery for the writer to carry.
The paste was hurting the writer's hands.
The cabbage was too cold for the writer to hold.
qs.why: 고춧가루 양념이 손을 빨갛고 화끈거리게 해서 장갑을 줬어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “It” in “It made my hands red and hot” refers to
qs.why: 앞 문장에서 만든 “a thick paste”를 가리켜요.

qs.q: In the last sentence, “eager” means
qs.why: “I am eager to taste the result”는 결과를 빨리 맛보고 싶어 들뜬 마음이에요.

items.title: The Broken Kite
items.text: Eun-ho had spent three evenings building a kite from paper and thin sticks. On Sunday, he carried it to the hill behind his apartment. The wind was perfect, and the kite rose higher than the trees. Then a sudden gust pulled the string out of his hand. The kite spun, hit a branch, and tore in the middle. Eun-ho felt his face grow hot. A girl who was flying her kite nearby walked over. "Don't throw it away," she said. "I have tape, and my father showed me a trick." Together they fixed the tear and added a long tail. The kite flew again, a little crooked, but Eun-ho thought it looked even better than before.

qs.q: What is the story mainly about?
o: A boy gave up flying kites forever.
A boy learned kite-making from his father.
A girl helped a boy repair his kite.
Two children had a kite race on a hill.
qs.why: 찢어진 연을 한 소녀가 도와 고쳐 준 이야기예요.

qs.q: What happened right before the kite tore?
qs.why: “The kite spun, hit a branch, and tore in the middle.” 줄은 끊어진 것이 아니라 손에서 빠져나갔어요.

qs.q: How did Eun-ho probably feel when the kite tore?
qs.why: 연이 찢어졌고 “his face grow hot”이라고 했으니 속상하고 당황했을 거예요.

qs.q: In the passage, “it” in “Don't throw it away” refers to
qs.why: 소녀가 버리지 말라고 한 것은 찢어진 연이에요.

qs.q: In the last sentence, “crooked” means
qs.why: “a little crooked”는 약간 삐뚤어진 모습이에요.

items.title: How Bats Find Their Way
items.text: Bats are active at night, when it is too dark to see well. So how do they avoid trees and catch insects? Many bats use sound. As they fly, they make very high squeaks that people usually cannot hear. The sound travels through the air, hits an object, and bounces back as an echo. The bat's ears catch the echo, and its brain uses it to tell how far away the object is and how big it is. This ability is called echolocation. Some bats can even notice an insect as thin as a hair. Scientists have studied this ability for many years.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why bats sleep upside down all day
Why people cannot hear very high squeaks
How bats use sound to find their way
How insects escape from hunting bats
qs.why: 박쥐가 소리와 메아리로 길을 찾는 방법을 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What happens to the sound a bat makes?
o: It is heard clearly by people.
qs.why: “hits an object, and bounces back as an echo.”

qs.q: Which task would be hardest for a bat that could not hear well?
o: Hanging upside down from a branch
Flying around in a bright room
qs.why: 박쥐는 메아리를 귀로 듣고 물체를 찾으므로, 잘 듣지 못하면 어둠 속에서 곤충을 찾기 어려워요.

qs.q: In the passage, “avoid” means
qs.why: “avoid trees”는 나무를 피한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: “This ability” in the passage refers to
o: making sounds that all people can hear
using echoes to learn about objects
seeing small things well in the dark
catching insects with the feet and wings
qs.why: 바로 앞에서 설명한 소리의 메아리로 물체의 거리와 크기를 아는 능력을 가리키고, 이것을 echolocation이라 불러요.

items.title: Problem with Order 4821
items.text:
Subject: Problem with Order 4821

Hello,

I ordered a green rain jacket from your website on October 2. It arrived yesterday, but there is a problem. I chose size medium, and the label inside says small. I tried it on, and the sleeves are too short for me. I have not worn it outside, and the tags are still attached. I would like to exchange it for the correct size. If medium is no longer in stock, I would prefer a refund. Please let me know how to send the jacket back. I hope you can answer before this weekend because I need the jacket for a school trip on Monday.

Thank you,
Dana Kim

qs.q: Why is Dana writing this email?
o: To complain about a very late delivery
To ask the shop to replace a jacket
To ask the shop for a discount on a coat
To thank the shop for its fast service
qs.why: Dana는 잘못된 사이즈의 재킷을 바꾸고 싶어서 편지를 썼어요.

qs.q: What is wrong with the jacket?
o: It arrived with a torn sleeve and no tags.
It has been worn outside by Dana already.
It costs more than the website said it would.
It is a different size from the one ordered.
qs.why: “I chose size medium, and the label inside says small.”

qs.q: What will Dana probably do if size medium is sold out?
qs.why: “If medium is no longer in stock, I would prefer a refund.”

qs.q: In the email, “exchange” means
qs.why: “exchange it for the correct size”는 올바른 사이즈로 교환한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “it” in “I tried it on” refers to
qs.why: 입어 본 것은 주문한 재킷이에요.

items.title: Join the Community Garden
items.text:
Join the Hillside Community Garden!

We have twelve small plots open for the new season. Each plot is about two meters by three meters, and it costs ten dollars for the whole year. Gardeners can grow vegetables, herbs, or flowers, but no tall trees are allowed because they would block the sun for others. Water is free, and tools are kept in the blue shed. Beginners are welcome. Every first Saturday, an experienced gardener will teach a short lesson at nine o'clock. To sign up, fill out the form at the Hillside Community Center desk before March 1. If more than twelve people apply, names will be chosen by lottery.

qs.q: What is the purpose of this notice?
o: To ask for money to buy new tools
To invite people to rent garden space
To explain how to grow herbs at home
To announce a garden flower contest
qs.why: 새 시즌에 텃밭 구역을 신청하라고 안내하는 글이에요.

qs.q: How can people sign up?
o: By filling out a form at the center
By writing a letter to a gardener
By paying ten dollars at the blue shed
By joining a lesson on Saturday morning
qs.why: “fill out the form at the Hillside Community Center desk before March 1.”

qs.q: What will happen if fifteen people apply?
o: The yearly price will go up.
The garden will add three more plots.
Some applicants will not get a plot.
Each person will get a smaller plot.
qs.why: 구역은 열두 개뿐이고 신청자가 더 많으면 추첨하므로 일부는 구역을 받지 못해요.

qs.q: In the notice, “plots” means
qs.why: “twelve small plots… two meters by three meters”는 작은 땅 구역을 말해요.

qs.q: In the passage, “they” in “because they would block the sun” refers to
qs.why: “no tall trees are allowed because they would block the sun”에서 they는 tall trees예요.

items.title: A Weekend on the Farm
items.text: My cousin Jisu lives on a small farm, and last weekend I stayed with her family. On Saturday I woke up at six because a rooster was shouting under my window. After breakfast, Jisu showed me how to collect eggs. I was nervous because the hens looked angry, but they did not mind. In the afternoon, we fed the goats and cleaned their pen, which smelled terrible. By evening my arms ached, yet I felt happy. At night I could see more stars than I had ever seen in the city. Before I left on Sunday, Jisu's mother gave me a basket of apples. I already want to go back during the summer vacation.

qs.q: How did the writer feel about the visit?
qs.why: 팔이 아팠지만 “I felt happy”, 또 “I already want to go back”이라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why did the writer wake up at six?
o: The goats needed to be fed.
Jisu asked for help with eggs.
qs.why: “a rooster was shouting under my window.”

qs.q: Where does the writer probably live?
qs.why: “more stars than I had ever seen in the city”라고 했으니 평소 도시에 사는 것으로 짐작할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “ached” means
qs.why: 일을 한 뒤 “my arms ached”는 팔이 아팠다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “they” in “but they did not mind” refers to
qs.why: 화난 듯 보였던 hens를 가리켜요.

items.title: Why Leaves Change Color
items.text: In autumn, many trees turn red, yellow, or orange before their leaves fall. The color change begins with the weather. During spring and summer, leaves are full of chlorophyll, a green substance that helps the tree turn sunlight into food. When the days become shorter and cooler, the tree stops making chlorophyll. The green slowly fades, and other colors that were hiding underneath become visible. Yellow and orange are always in the leaf; we just cannot see them until the green disappears. Red is a little different. Some trees make new red coloring in autumn when bright, cool days follow each other. After the colors have faded, the leaves turn brown and drop to the ground.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Which trees are the most beautiful ones
Why leaves turn different colors in autumn
How trees grow new leaves in spring
Why some trees keep their leaves all year
qs.why: 가을에 잎 색이 변하는 이유를 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What does chlorophyll help a tree do?
qs.why: “a green substance that helps the tree turn sunlight into food.”

qs.q: What would probably happen if autumn days stayed long and warm?
o: Leaves would fall off in summer.
Leaves would turn red much sooner.
Trees would stop making any food.
qs.why: 해가 짧아지고 서늘해지면 엽록소가 줄어든다고 했으니, 길고 따뜻하면 초록색이 더 오래 남을 거예요.

qs.q: In the passage, “fades” means
qs.why: “The green slowly fades”는 초록색이 점점 옅어진다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “them” in “we just cannot see them” refers to
qs.why: 앞 문장 “Yellow and orange are always in the leaf”의 색깔들을 가리켜요.

items.title: The Substitute Bus Driver
items.text: Every morning, Mr. Cho greeted us with a joke when we climbed onto the school bus. On Thursday, a different driver was behind the wheel. She did not smile, and she held the steering wheel tightly. "Mr. Cho is sick," she said. "I am Ms. Lee, and this is my first day on this route." At the third corner, she turned left instead of right. Nobody spoke for a moment. Then Yuna stood up and said, "Excuse me, we usually turn right at the bakery." Ms. Lee thanked her, and soon the students were calling out directions together. When we reached school, she finally smiled and said, "Tomorrow, I will bring a joke of my own."

qs.q: What is the story mainly about?
o: A bus broke down on the road.
Mr. Cho told a funny joke.
A driver lost her job at a school.
Students helped a worried new driver.
qs.why: 처음 노선을 운전하는 불안한 기사님을 학생들이 도와준 이야기예요.

qs.q: Why was there a new driver?
o: The students asked for a change.
qs.why: “Mr. Cho is sick.”

qs.q: Why did Ms. Lee hold the steering wheel tightly?
o: She was cold in the early morning.
She was angry at the noisy students.
She wanted to drive very fast to school.
She felt nervous about the new route.
qs.why: 그날이 이 노선의 첫날이라고 했고 웃지 않았으니 긴장했다고 짐작할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “route” means
o: a rule for all the students
a seat near the front door
qs.why: “first day on this route”는 버스가 다니는 길을 뜻해요.

qs.q: In the passage, “her” in “Ms. Lee thanked her” refers to
qs.why: 길을 알려 준 학생 Yuna에게 고마워한 거예요.

items.title: Old Phones, New Life
items.text: Many people replace their phones every two or three years. The old phones often end up in a drawer or in the trash. This is a problem because phones contain metals such as copper and small amounts of gold. When phones are thrown away, these metals are wasted, and harmful materials may enter the soil. Recycling centers solve part of the problem. Workers take the phones apart, remove the battery, and separate the metals so that they can be used again. Some schools and shops also collect old phones to give them to people who cannot afford a new one. Before giving away a phone, you should delete your photos and messages. Doing this takes only a few minutes, and it keeps your private information safe.

qs.q: Why did the writer write this article?
o: To explain why old phones should be recycled
To compare phones from two shops
To advertise a new kind of phone
To teach people how to fix phones
qs.why: 오래된 휴대폰을 재활용해야 하는 이유와 방법을 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What should people do before giving away a phone?
qs.why: “you should delete your photos and messages.”

qs.q: What can be inferred about old phones kept in drawers?
o: They harm the soil around them.
They cannot be recycled at all.
Their metals are not being reused.
qs.why: 서랍 속 휴대폰은 재활용되지 않으므로 그 안의 금속도 다시 쓰이지 않아요.

qs.q: In the passage, “separate” means
qs.why: “separate the metals”는 금속을 분리한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “them” in “to give them to people” refers to
qs.why: 학교와 가게가 모아서 나누어 주는 것은 old phones예요.

items.title: Question About the Science Report
items.text:
Subject: Question about the science report

Dear Mr. Han,

I hope you are well. I am writing to ask about the science report that is due on Friday. I was absent from school on Tuesday and Wednesday because I had the flu, and I missed the lesson about experiments. My doctor said I should rest until Thursday. I have started the report, but I cannot finish the experiment part without watching the demonstration again. Would it be possible to hand in my report on Monday instead? I know that is a lot to ask. I will also come to your room at lunchtime on Thursday if you have time to explain the lesson to me.

Sincerely,
Minji

qs.q: Why is Minji writing to Mr. Han?
o: To say a lesson was canceled
To ask for a new report topic
qs.why: Minji는 아파서 수업을 놓쳤고 보고서를 월요일에 내도 되는지 물어보고 있어요.

qs.q: When does Minji offer to visit Mr. Han's room?
qs.why: “I will also come to your room at lunchtime on Thursday.”

qs.q: Why is the experiment part difficult for Minji?
o: She lost her notebook at home.
She does not like science class.
She started the report too late.
She did not see the demonstration in class.
qs.why: 실험 수업을 놓쳐서 시연을 다시 보지 않으면 그 부분을 끝낼 수 없다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the email, “hand in” means
qs.why: “hand in my report”는 보고서를 제출한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “that” in “I know that is a lot to ask” refers to
o: handing in the report on Monday
qs.why: 바로 앞 질문인 월요일에 제출해도 되는지를 가리켜요.

items.title: Learning to Swim at Fifteen
items.text: Most of my friends learned to swim when they were five, but I never did. I was always afraid of deep water, and I made excuses at every pool party. This summer I decided to change that. I joined a beginners' class at the community pool, where I was the tallest student by far. At first, I felt embarrassed when children half my size floated easily. My teacher, however, never made me feel silly. She told me to breathe out slowly under the water and trust my body to rise. It took three weeks before I could float for ten seconds. Last Saturday, I swam across the shallow end without stopping. I think being brave means doing something frightening, even if you do it slowly.

qs.q: What is the writer's main point at the end?
o: Pool parties are never any fun.
Being brave can mean doing a scary thing slowly.
Swimming is easy once you begin to practice.
Children learn faster than older students do.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 무서운 일을 천천히 하더라도 하는 것이 용기라고 말해요.

qs.q: How long did it take before the writer could float for ten seconds?
qs.why: “It took three weeks before I could float for ten seconds.”

qs.q: Why did the writer feel embarrassed at first?
o: The class was too expensive to join.
The other students were much smaller.
The pool was very crowded that day.
qs.why: 키가 가장 큰 학생이었고 절반 크기의 아이들이 쉽게 뜨는 것을 봤기 때문이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “silly” means
qs.why: “never made me feel silly”는 바보 같다고 느끼게 하지 않았다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “She” in “She told me to breathe out slowly” refers to
qs.why: 바로 앞의 “My teacher”를 가리켜요.

items.title: Changes at Eastgate Station
items.text:
Attention Passengers

Because of track work, there will be changes at Eastgate Station from Saturday, May 10, through Sunday, May 18. Trains to Lakeview usually leave from Platform 2, but during this time they will use Platform 5. To reach Platform 5, use the stairs by the ticket office or take the elevator near the east exit. Trains to the airport will run every twenty minutes instead of every ten. Please allow extra time for your trip. Station staff in orange vests will be on every platform to help you, and printed maps are available at the information desk. Passengers who use wheelchairs may ask for help at the desk. We are sorry for any inconvenience.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this notice?
o: To tell passengers about temporary changes
To sell tickets for a new line
To ask for volunteers at the desk
To close the station for good
qs.why: 선로 공사 때문에 일정 기간 바뀌는 사항을 알리는 안내문이에요.

qs.q: Which platform will Lakeview trains use during the work?
qs.why: “during this time they will use Platform 5.”

qs.q: What can a traveler to the airport expect during the work?
qs.why: 공항행 열차가 10분 간격에서 20분 간격으로 바뀌므로 더 오래 기다려야 해요.

qs.q: In the notice, “allow extra time” means
qs.why: “Please allow extra time”은 여유 시간을 더 잡으라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, “they” in “they will use Platform 5” refers to
qs.why: 앞부분의 “Trains to Lakeview”를 가리켜요.
